A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MambaIC and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. All 12 pages of each version support comparison; both supplementary pages are visually identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-compression experiments, including rate-distortion results, latency measurements, component ablations, and supplementary architecture comparisons.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments in Figures 4–7, Tables 1–4, and the supplementary material.

M1.justification: Figure 2 replaces attention/residual-block transforms with VSS-block transforms and revises convolution kernels and repetitions. However, v1 already describes SSM-based main transforms in Section 3.2 and Appendix D/Table A2. The unchanged method prose leaves unclear whether this revises the implemented architecture or corrects its depiction.

E1.justification: Flickr30k training, Kodak, Tecnick and CLIC Professional Valid evaluation, and the resolution-scaling scenarios are retained without coverage changes.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain ELIC, Mixed, MLIC, Entroformer, Contextformer, MambaVC, BPG and VTM/VVC. Mixed's changed scores do not establish a changed comparator; the newly cited PPT work is not evaluated.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation procedures and settings remain unchanged, including metrics, 250 training epochs, channel counts, five channel chunks, image cropping and evaluation hardware. No revised experimental protocol is stated for the changed Mixed results.

E4.justification: Component ablations, CNN/Transformer/SSM comparisons, window-size analysis and qualitative attention-map studies are unchanged, including Tables 2–4, Table A2 and Figures A1–A2.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes only Mixed's row: encoding latency 154.41 to 127.36 ms, decoding latency 107.24 to 91.44 ms, FLOPS 415.20 to 211.54 G, and BD-rate −9.65% to −7.39%. MambaIC and the other experimental results remain unchanged. The reason for these numerical revisions is not stated.

T1.justification: Equations 1–14, including the compression objective, SSM discretization, context modeling and attention formulation, are unchanged. No assumptions, proofs or derivations are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about integrating SSMs into transforms and context modeling, adding local attention, and improving compression efficiency and high-resolution performance.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations, ablation interpretations and applicability statements are unchanged, with no new substantive limitations. Section 4.4 retains its old Mixed comparison despite the revised table values.

D1.justification: Figure 2 revises the documented transform construction: four RB/5×5 stages become an outer 5×5 layer and three VSS/3×3 stages, and the residual-block detail inset disappears. These are documentation changes whose implementation status is unclear. Training details, hardware and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Wu et al., 'PPT: Token Pruning and Pooling for Efficient Vision Transformers,' to the compression-background sentence in Section 2.2 and the references. Other citation changes are renumbering; the research positioning is otherwise unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes are limited to the arXiv version/date stamp, citation renumbering and small text reflow around the added reference. The prose, section organization and appendix structure are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: Figure 2 redraws the main transforms and removes the residual-block inset while retaining the overall schematic arrangement. Other figures and table structures are unchanged; Table 1 changes numerical entries only.

improvement.justification: Figure 2 better aligns with the existing SSM description, but the PDFs do not explain whether its architecture revisions are corrections or implementation changes, and its caption still mentions residual bottleneck blocks. Table 1 also introduces a discrepancy: the revised Mixed–MambaIC BD-rate gap is 5.13 percentage points, while Section 4.4 retains 2.87. These competing effects on clarity and consistency prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
